svg.title: From a commit to Cape Town
svg.desc: From a commit to Cape Town, in three lanes: Laptop, GitHub (KatlehoKomeke/Appointment-Booking-System) and AWS. Everything drawn is built. Step A, along the top: the administrator, branchbook-admin signed in with aws login, runs cdk deploy BranchbookAccount and BranchbookGuardrails by hand; the edge leads to BranchbookAccount in us-east-1. Laptop: git commit. Step 1, the pre-commit hook refuses secret files, then runs gitleaks on the staged diff; it fails closed, and a refused edge leads to 'commit refused'. The post-commit hook prints a reminder only. Then git push, the start of the main path, which crosses into GitHub. A caveat note joined to both hooks: they are opt-in (make hooks), and --no-verify skips the pre-commit hook. GitHub: push protection refuses known provider secrets; a refused edge leads to 'push rejected'. Step 2, main, a gate: the ruleset Protect main starts the workflows, requires every check before a push or merge to main, and refuses a force-push. From it, three more workflows: codeql.yml, static analysis; dependency-review.yml, on pull requests only; and secret-scan.yml, gitleaks over the full history, which cannot block a push. Below them, Dependabot opens weekly pull requests, on which the checks run and nothing is delivered; and aws-connection-check.yml runs by hand as either environment's role. The main path enters ci.yml, whose checks have no AWS access: api, web, infra and workflow-lint, and step 3, image, which builds the ARM64 image once, then stack, which runs the end-to-end tests, k6 and ZAP against that same image. Once every check is green on a push to main, the main path continues through the delivery jobs. Step 4, publish, in the staging environment, pushes the image to ECR and attests its provenance and SBOM; its digest is what every later job deploys. Step 5, deploy-staging, deploys that digest to staging, runs the smoke and end-to-end tests there and records the release. A gate, approval: the production environment needs a person's approval. Step 6, deploy-production, verifies the image's provenance, deploys the same digest to production, smoke-tests it and records the release. If it fails, rollback-production redeploys the previous release; a caveat note says the rollback waits for the same approval. AWS: every delivery job signs in through OpenID Connect via AWS STS, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, with no stored keys; a dotted line joins STS to the role it trusts. In AWS · us-east-1 (N. Virginia), the BranchbookAccount stack holds the OIDC provider, the budget and the deploy roles branchbook-github-deploy-staging and branchbook-github-deploy-production, one per environment. In AWS · af-south-1 (Cape Town): publish deploys the stack BranchbookRegistry, the ECR repository with immutable tags; deploy-staging updates staging at stg.branchbook.click, the stacks BranchbookStagingData, BranchbookStagingApp and BranchbookStagingRelease; the main path ends at production, highlighted, at branchbook.click, the stacks BranchbookData, BranchbookApp and BranchbookRelease, which deploy-production and rollback-production update. Last, BranchbookGuardrails, deployed by hand, holds the audit trail and the limits on every deployment. Legend: Built; Main path; Refused or not allowed; Gap or caveat; AWS category: security.
